Summer rules for the arrivals team
This section explains the steps that matter
Companion Animal Travel Desk Summer Control

This section sets the urgent handling rules for companion animal arrivals, with strict attention to safety, calm transfer, and clean handoff at every point. All staff must keep the carrier in view, confirm documents at once, and guide the traveler without delay so the animal does not face avoidable stress. Aurelia Skyways expects the desk to keep movement orderly and to pass each case to the ground team only after checks are complete.

All arrivals with animals must be reviewed before transfer, and any missing item must be reported at once to the senior coordinator. The traveler must remain informed in direct language, but staff must not speculate or improvise on the route, the holding area, or the condition of the animal. <<FACT F020>> The carrier must stay closed unless a licensed handler opens it for inspection, and the desk must note any signs of distress, damage, or contamination without delay. If the traveler requests help, staff must respond promptly and keep the exchange brief, formal, and respectful.

Quarantine cases demand even tighter control. <<FACT F029>> No animal may be released to a public area until the required review is finished and the record is cleared by the designated authority. The ground team must move carriers carefully between services, maintain separation from general baggage, and keep hands washed and surfaces clean after each transfer. Any mismatch between the papers, the label, and the animal in the carrier must halt the process immediately. Staff must not leave an animal unattended, even for a short interval, and must not accept verbal assurances in place of written clearance.

When a case is unstable, the desk must secure the area, call the senior coordinator, and wait for direct instruction before taking further action. All reports must be plain, complete, and immediate. Contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor at once for any unresolved companion animal travel concern.
